In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in adult rat SPG neuron, the activation of M(3) mAChR is responsible for desensitization and internalization of MOR.
the M(2)-opioid interaction in the SPG neurons is a complex phenomenon that involves both heterologous and homologous desenstization of these receptors.
in adult rat SPG neuronal preparations, M(2)mAChR and MOR couple to Galpha(i/o)-mediated Ca(2+) channel inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of M(3) mAChR and MOR are coupled with the same Galpha(q) protein subunits to mediate Ca(2+) channel activation in rat sphenopalantine ganglion neurons.
M(2) and MOR are coupled to Galpha(i/o), and the M(2)-MOR coupling mechanism may be involved in regulating cerebral blood flow.
M(2) and MOR are expressed in rat SPG and their activation results in inhibition of Ca(+) currents via Galpha(i/o)-mediated pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of M2 mAChRs can modulate opioid transmission in the SPG neurons.
the M2 mAChR can modulate the opioid response of the SPG neurons, and that this effect is not due to a direct interaction between the M2 mAChr and the mu opioid receptors.
the activation of M2 mAChRs leads to desensitization and functional uncoupling of the MOR, thus providing a novel target for therapeutic interventions in the brain vascculature.
